correctness.rationale: All assertions are for finite-dimensional evolution algebras over algebraically closed fields of characteristic not two with one-dimensional square. Multiplication is exactly B(x,y)v. The annihilator equals rad(B), and natural-basis vectors with zero square are exactly its radical basis vectors. The three conditions on |S intersect T| follow from v in rad(B) or the value B(v,v). Witt extension gives all possible nonzero active supports of a fixed norm, including isotropic cases, and radical translations independently realize any radical support. Every natural-basis graph has active source set T and identical nonempty out-neighborhood S. Counting T and subsets gives the labeled and unlabeled formulas and the simultaneous-family criterion. The packaged exact checker constructs 124 permitted patterns and checks Gram congruence, support and counts, without relying on these tests as infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The current statement is an explicit complete classification of all graph supports from natural bases of each rank-one-square algebra, including precise attainment and counting, directly addressing the restricted form of Question 30 of arXiv:2610.22248. residual_risks: A graph-spectrum conclusion could be treated as an implicit consequence of 2020 natural-basis or 2025 pointed-quadratic-space classifications; human priority assessment is still warranted.

value.rationale: The rank-one-square family is a natural infinite class of nonperfect evolution algebras for which the structure graph depends on natural basis. The theorem resolves the full simultaneous graph realization question inside this class, proves a sharp active-support threshold distinguishing two intrinsically different square-zero cases, and gives exact labeled and unlabeled counts for arbitrary dimension and radical size. These are structural invariants of all bases of a fixed algebra, not an arbitrary numerical slice or known table recomputation.
